label: Multi-layered wall with air gap, functions only (EN)
english: The wall element is overall 25 cm thick, with a multi-layered wall, where the in-between layer is an air gap of 5 cm, the outer layer is 5 cm facade, and inner layer is 15 cm load bearing.

matches.text: MultiLayer | Multi Layer | A wall assembly with several distinct layers, often combining structure, insulation, and cladding (e.g., sandwich panels).
SingleLayer | Single Layer | A solid, monolithic wall construction without separate cavities or insulation layers.

Brick | Material Category: Brick / Ceramics
What it is made of / How it's made: It is made from natural surface clay, shale, or refined earthen minerals mixed with water. This plastic mixture is shaped into blocks and dried before being baked in a high-temperature kiln, which triggers a chemical sintering process that fuses the mineral particles into a durable, vitrified, rock-hard structure.
Description: A traditional, rectangular masonry building block manufactured from raw earthen clays or silicates and hardened by extreme heat or chemical bonding, used for building structural walls and facades (Brick). | https://www.iso.org/standard/32918.html
Frame | A skeletal or frame structure of wood or steel.

HeavyWeightAggregate | Heavy Weight Aggregate | HeavyWeightAggregate | What it is made of / How it's made: It is made by mining natural, high-density minerals and metallic ores—such as Barite, Magnetite, Hematite, or Ilmenite—or by utilizing manufactured industrial bi-products like steel shot. These raw materials are crushed and strictly graded to maintain a specific gravity significantly higher than standard gravel (typically above 3.5 to 6.0).
Description: A specialized, ultra-high-density category of loose mineral aggregates engineered explicitly to add mass and block radiation when mixed into heavy-duty composite structures.

LightWeightAggregate | Light Weight Aggregate | What it is made of / How it's made: It is made by minerally processing natural volcanic rocks (like pumice or scoria) or by thermally expanding raw clays, shales, or slates inside a high-temperature rotary kiln. The rapid heating causes embedded gases to expand, bloating the mineral structure into porous, structural pellets with a highly cellular, air-trapping internal matrix.
Description: A specialized category of low-density, highly porous mineral aggregates engineered to drastically reduce dead weight and enhance thermal insulation when substituted for standard stone or gravel in composite matrices.

BrickMasonryUnit | Brick Masonry Unit | BrickMasonryUnit | Material Category: Brick / Ceramics
What it is made of / How it's made: It is made from natural surface clay, shale, or refined earthen minerals mixed with water. It is pressed or extruded into a rectangular block shape and then dried and baked in a high-temperature kiln until the minerals chemically fuse into a vitrified, rock-hard structure.
Description: A standard, kiln-fired rectangular building block used for laying structural or facing brickwork (BrickMasonryUnit). | https://www.iso.org/standard/32918.html

Aggregates | Mineral Aggregates & Fillers | Material Category: Mineral Aggregates & Fillers
What it is made of / How it's made: It is made from natural geological deposits of sand, gravel, and heavy minerals, or from crushed rock and industrial by-products. These loose particles are mechanically washed, crushed, and strictly graded by particle size and density without altering their inherent chemical composition.
Description: A category of loose, chemically inert granular materials (ranging from fine sand to coarse gravel and high-density heavyweight minerals) that provide the bulk volume, structural stability, and compressive mass within composite matrices like concrete and mortar.
Cavity | Two masonry leaves separated by an air space (cavity), sometimes filled with insulation to prevent moisture and heat loss.
